summary: Sustained P99 latency regressions after batcher weighting change introduced sticky microbatches
description:
Issue summary: Starting 2026-03-10 02:10 UTC customers observed sustained P99 inference latency regressions (2x-4x baseline) and increased request timeouts (504) across multiple Hosted API routes. Root cause suspected to be a recently deployed continuous-batcher weighting change that was intended to favor short sequences.

Impact: Multiple self-serve and dedicated customers experienced increased tail latency impacting user-facing chat UIs and background batch jobs. Error rate increased ~0.6% (5xx/504) on affected routes. Not a full outage, but regressions exceed SLOs and triggered CS escalations.

Environment: prod us-east and prod eu-west; Redwood hosted API; affected models: gpt-4o-mini, redwood-instruct-7B, community/llama-3-13B.

Steps to reproduce: 1) Simulate mixed workload (60% short requests <50 tokens, 40% long sequences >400 tokens) against a single connection pool. 2) Observe batcher metrics: average batch size, microbatch count, batch wait_time distribution. 3) After the daytime traffic ramp, P99 token latency climbs and long sequence requests form small, serialized microbatches.

Observed behavior: Instead of grouping long sequences into efficient batches, requests with long sequences are repeatedly isolated into 1-2 request microbatches and held waiting for a per-connection weight timer to decay. This creates head-of-line sequences that then expand processing latency for downstream requests due to KV cache eviction patterns.

Relevant configuration changes: 2026-03-09 23:45 UTC deploy: batcher policy "weight_short_first_v2" enabled; change introduced per-connection short-request weighting and a weight_decay window (default 30s).
impact: P99 latency increased 2-4x on affected routes; 504 timeouts rose by ~0.6% for impacted tenants; SLAs at risk for enterprise customers on Dedicated; increased support volume
steps_to_reproduce: Create mixed-load traffic: 60% requests with short context (<50 tokens), 40% with long context (>400 tokens) to the same API key and connection pool
Look for sustained small batch sizes for long-sequence requests and rising p99_token_latency in tracing
logs:
[2026-03-10T02:12:03Z] batcher(pool=pool-42) INFO microbatch_created size=1 reason=weight_priority
[2026-03-10T02:12:03Z] request(id=abc123) DEBUG seq_len=512 kv_cache_miss=true
[2026-03-10T02:12:28Z] serving-runtime WARN token_latency p99=1.2s (baseline 0.45s)
[2026-03-10T02:14:05Z] proxy ERROR upstream_timeout code=504 route=/v1/generate customer=AcmeCorp
comments: 2026-03-10 Maya Chen (Support): Customer AcmeCorp reported intermittent UI stalls; they provided request IDs and timeframe. Escalated to SRE oncall.

2026-03-10 Ravi Patel (SRE): Noted recent deployment "weight_short_first_v2" at 2026-03-09 23:45 UTC. Initial hypothesis: new weighting favors short sequences but weight_decay not expiring as expected, causing stickiness.

2026-03-11 Priya Kapoor (Eng): Reproduced locally with mixed traffic; observed microbatch_count dominated by 1-2 request batches for long sequences. Added extended logging for per-connection weight timers.
2026-03-12 Ravi Patel (SRE): Rolled back weight_short_first_v2 on canary, observed P99 drop back to baseline in canary region within 12 minutes. Planning global rollback pending QA.
investigation_notes: 2026-03-10 04:00 UTC: SRE captured timeline correlating deploy to spike onset (+~25 minutes).

2026-03-10 06:20 UTC: Heap of long-seq requests tied to per-connection priority value that never reached zero due to integer underflow in the decay calculation when connection_idle_ms > 2^31 ms (edge cases in legacy pool reset path).

2026-03-11 09:10 UTC: Reproduced an edge-case where a connection that had seen a flurry of short requests retained high short-weight and blocked long requests from being coalesced into multi-request batches.
2026-03-11 11:30 UTC: Canary rollback validated; metrics: p99_token_latency reduced from 1.1s -> 0.48s; timeout rate reduced to baseline.
root_cause: Bug in batcher weight_decay calculation introduced by "weight_short_first_v2" deploy: weight value could underflow and then saturate positive (sticky) due to integer wrap, causing per-connection priority to prefer short-request treatment indefinitely and fragment long-sequence batching.
resolution:
Immediate: Rolled back weight_short_first_v2 globally at 2026-03-12 02:40 UTC. Post-rollback the p99 latency and timeout rates returned to baseline in ~15 minutes for most pools.

Workaround for customers: Route heavy long-sequence workloads to Dedicated pools (untouched) or increase client-side concurrency to distribute across more connection pools until fix deployed.

Permanent fix: Patch weight_decay calculation to use saturating subtraction with 64-bit signed arithmetic and add unit tests covering long-idle pools and high-traffic churn. Fix PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/7852. Plan: deploy canary + staged rollout + increase monitoring for microbatch_count, weight_timer_stale_count.

Follow-ups: Add synthetic regression test in CI that mixes short/long workloads; add alert when long-sequence avg_batch_size < 1.5 and p99_token_latency > baseline*1.5 for >10 minutes.
